highlights: Thinking Machines Lab released Inkling 2 Mini, a multimodal Mixture-of-Experts model with ~26B total and 3B active parameters per token, a 1M-token context size, and image and text inputs.
Apple's Depth Pro 2 estimates dense metric depth at native resolution for images and video, releasing a model family plus code and weights.
WeMM-Video is a family of Chinese-English bilingual omni-modal foundation models spanning 2B, 4B, 9B, and 35B-A3B variants, with the WeMM-Video family publicly released.

items.title: Thinking Machines Lab releases Inkling 2 Mini multimodal model
items.summary: Inkling 2 Mini is a new looped transformer model and a multimodal Mixture-of-Experts with ~26B physical total and 3B active parameters per token, supporting a 1M-token context size with image and text inputs. Thinking Machines Lab ships it in a mixed-precision format with NVFP4 and MXFP8 expert weights, alongside transformers, Llama App (llama.cpp), and MLX support, with day-zero SGLang inference support for datacenter hardware.

evidence.quote: TLDR; Inkling 2 Mini is a new looped transformer model.
It’s a multimodal Mixture-of-Experts with ~26B physical total and 3B active parameters per token.
It uses a neat trick to increase capacity: some layers are visited in a loop that repeats three times, which makes it work like it had more parameters.
It supports a 1M-token context size, accepts images and text inputs.
Thinking Machines Lab ships the model in a mixed-precision format, with NVFP4 and MXFP8 expert weights.
We ship transformers, Llama App (llama.cpp), and MLX support.
SGLang also provides day-zero inference support for production deployments on datacenter hardware.

items.title: Apple presents Depth Pro 2 for metric monocular depth
items.summary: Depth Pro 2 is an approach to estimating dense metric depth for images and video at full resolution, using a single scalable network that handles both and predicts depth maps at native resolution. It produces depth maps that are metrically accurate, sharp, and temporally consistent at once, and Apple releases a family of models plus code and weights.

evidence.quote: Richter, Vladlen Koltun View publication View source code (GitHub) Copy Bibtex We present Depth Pro 2, an approach to estimating dense metric depth for images and video at full resolution.

By analyzing prior methods for monocular depth estimation, we find that they commonly trade off temporal consistency and boundary sharpness: multi-frame methods favor consistency, single-frame methods favor sharpness.
To overcome this trade-off, we train a single, scalable network that processes both images and video and predicts depth maps at native resolution.
Depth Pro 2 produces depth maps that are metrically accurate, sharp, and temporally consistent all at once, outperforming prior work in all of these dimensions.
We release a family of models that define a new Pareto frontier in terms of metric accuracy, sharpness, temporal consistency, and runtime.
We release code and weights here .
Depth Pro 2 estimates the depth of every pixel, in meters, from images taken with an ordinary camera.
One network handles a single photo, a whole video, or a live camera feed, at the input’s full resolution.
Its depth is sharp at object edges and steady from frame to frame.

items.title: OpenAI details a layered defense against adversarial distillation
items.summary: OpenAI's approach combines adversarial testing, model training, classifiers, and API-level protections with investigations into coordinated attempts to extract model capabilities. In an internal adaptive evaluation, the average attack success rate fell from 54.0% against GPT‑6 Astra with its original safeguards to 0.2% against GPT‑6.2 Astra with its updated safeguards.

evidence.quote: Adversarial distillation creates a path for bad actors to reproduce these capabilities without appropriate safeguards.

Our approach to adversarial distillation combines adversarial testing, model training, classifiers, and API-level protections with investigations into coordinated attempts to extract model capabilities.

We place particular emphasis on preventing attackers from extracting our models’ protected reasoning: the intermediate steps a model generates internally while working toward an answer, known as its chain-of-thought.
In an internal adaptive evaluation using strong automated red-teaming , we tested whether attackers could recover protected reasoning the model had generated while answering an earlier prompt.
The average attack success rate fell from 54.0% against GPT‑6 Astra with its original safeguards to 0.2% against GPT‑6.2 Astra with its updated safeguards.
Defenses that reinforce one another We defend against adversarial distillation at two complementary levels of our safeguard stack.
Our defenses against adversarial distillation combine safeguards for individual requests with campaign detection and enforcement.

Classifier safeguards We use input classifiers to detect attempts to extract protected reasoning, and output classifiers to detect leaks of protected reasoning in assistant messages and tool-call arguments.

items.title: WeMM-Video open-sources bilingual omni-modal video models
items.summary: WeMM-Video is a family of Chinese-English bilingual omni-modal foundation models spanning 2B, 4B, 9B, and 35B-A3B variants, trained on a large-scale multimodal corpus of approximately 1.2 trillion tokens with both instruct and thinking modes. Evaluated across more than 120 benchmarks, the flagship WeMM-Video-35B-A3B substantially outperforms proprietary models such as Qwen3.5-Omni-Flash and Seed2.0-Mini-0428, and the family is publicly released with its evaluation and reproduction pipeline.

evidence.quote: In this report, we introduce WeMM-Video, a family of Chinese-English bilingual omni-modal foundation models spanning 2B, 4B, 9B, and 35B-A3B variants.

Centering on joint audio-visual perception and reasoning, WeMM-Video unifies text, image, audio, and video processing within a hybrid-thinking paradigm , seamlessly supporting both a non-thinking instruct mode for fast, direct responses and a thinking mode for explicit step-by-step reasoning .

The models are trained on a large-scale multimodal corpus of approximately 1.2 trillion tokens through progressive pre-training and a multi-stage post-training pipeline incorporating multi-teacher OPD , anti-repetition MrDPO , and specialist RL .

Evaluated across more than 120 benchmarks, WeMM-Video demonstrates superior performance in omni-modal video understanding and reasoning, while maintaining highly competitive capabilities across general audio, silent video, image, and text tasks.

Specifically, in omni-modal video evaluations, our flagship WeMM-Video-35B-A3B establishes a new open-source state of the art, substantially outperforming proprietary models such as Qwen3.5-Omni-Flash and Seed2.0-Mini-0428 while narrowing the gap with the strong Gemini-3.0-Flash, and our compact WeM
M-Video-9B surpasses the larger open-source Qwen3-Omni-30B-A3B-Instruct.
We publicly release the WeMM-Video family along with our evaluation and reproduction pipeline to foster further research and development in the open-source community.

items.title: Hugging Face trains per-harness LoRA adapters for Qwen3.8-27B
items.summary: The team trained one LoRA adapter for Qwen3.8-27B per agent harness (pi, Hermes Agent, OpenCode), with RL inside the harness itself, and merged the three LoRAs into a single super adapter that runs unchanged under pi, Hermes Agent and OpenCode. Each harness adapter beats the base model under its own harness on both performance and efficiency, and all artifacts, including adapters, GGUFs, RL tasks, and the safeagents plugin, can be browsed through a Hugging Face collection.

evidence.quote: Combining RL on a custom task distribution with your favorite agent harness yields more accurate and efficient models for that target harness and task distribution.
Take Qwen3.8-27B, its Terminal-Bench 2.1 score with the pi harness is 39% which uses on average 2.9K tokens per task.
If we freeze those weights and add a custom RL-trained LoRA adapter we can get 55% pass@1, with average token usage of 1.5K.
Most of this is down to the model reasoning less, calling less tools, and performing better first time.
Here we wanted to push this further by exploring whether the result holds at 27B, on harder real-world software engineering tasks, across three harnesses: Pi, OpenCode and Hermes Agent.
We trained one LoRA adapter for Qwen3.8-27B per agent harness (pi, Hermes Agent, OpenCode), with RL inside the harness itself.
Datasets, training and agent rollouts all happen on the Hub in Jobs using TRL's AsyncGRPOTrainer , OpenEnv and harbor.
Each harness adapter beats the base model under its own harness on both benchmarks, for both performance and efficiency.
The three LoRAs are also merged into a single super adapter that runs unchanged under pi, Hermes Agent and OpenCode.
All artifacts (adapters, GGUFs, RL tasks, safeagents plugin) can be browsed through this Hugging Face collection .

items.title: obra/superpowers adds a skills-based agent development methodology
items.summary: Superpowers is a software development methodology for coding agents built on composable skills and instructions that trigger automatically from the moment the agent starts a build. It guides the agent through a spec, an implementation plan, red/green TDD, and subagent-driven development, and it is available through the official Claude plugin marketplace and the official Codex plugin marketplace.

evidence.quote: Superpowers is a complete software development methodology for your coding agents, built on top of a set of composable skills and some initial instructions that make sure your agent uses them.
It starts from the moment you fire up your coding agent.
As soon as it sees that you're building something, it doesn't just jump into trying to write code.
Once it's teased a spec out of the conversation, it shows it to you in chunks short enough to actually read and digest.

After you've signed off on the design, your agent puts together an implementation plan that's clear enough for an enthusiastic junior engineer with poor taste, no judgement, no project context, and an aversion to testing to follow.
It emphasizes true red/green TDD, YAGNI (You Aren't Gonna Need It), and DRY.
Next up, once you say "go", it launches a subagent-driven-development process, having agents work through each engineering task, inspecting and reviewing their work, and continuing forward.
It's not uncommon for your agent to work autonomously for a couple hours at a time without deviating from the plan you put together.
And because the skills trigger automatically, you don't need to do anything special.

items.title: WeVisForensics detects AI-generated video with self-evolving agents
items.summary: WeVisForensics is an agentic framework in which a main investigator agent coordinates a self-evolving library of forensic inspector sub-agents spanning visual and audio cues, with DTPO using fast reinforcement learning for the investigator and slower refinement for the inspectors. It averages 95.2% detection accuracy across in-domain, out-of-domain and agentic benchmarks, 9.0% above the strongest prior detector, and the team curates ForenCue-30K for training and evaluation.

evidence.quote: We introduce WeVisForensics, an agentic framework in which a main investigator agent coordinates a self-evolving library of forensic inspector sub-agents spanning visual and audio cues .
The investigator learns which artifact type to examine, over which window, and when to conclude, and these interactions provide shared feedback for both levels of agents.

Our dual-timescale policy optimization strategy, DTPO , closes this loop through fast reinforcement learning of the investigator and slower refinement of the inspectors, guided by annotated artifact intervals , to report subtle artifacts they once dismissed.

Furthermore, we curate ForenCue-30K , combining role-specific forensic annotations and interaction trajectories to supervise individual inspections and their coordination, with an accompanying reinforcement-learning pool .

Experiments show that WeVisForensics averages 95.2% detection accuracy across in-domain, out-of-domain and agentic benchmarks, 9.0% above the strongest prior detector, while grounding its verdicts in localized evidence.

items.title: Mind2Act World diagnoses embodied reasoning and execution failures
items.summary: Mind2Act World is a diagnostic benchmark of 30 simulated manipulation tasks from five real-world application domains, with three difficulty levels and two scene settings (Clean and Random), yielding 180 configurations. Its Mind, Act, and Mind2Act views separate reasoning, execution, and their composition, and the strongest agent succeeds in 52.7% of Mind and 39.0% of Act episodes but in only 12.0% of Mind2Act episodes.

evidence.quote: We introduce Mind2Act World, a diagnostic benchmark of 30 simulated manipulation tasks from five real-world application domains.
Each task has three difficulty levels and two scene settings (Clean and Random), yielding 180 configurations.

The tasks form three views: Mind tests decisions based on past observations, Act tests precise and timely execution, and Mind2Act combines both in closed-loop tasks where action outcomes guide later decisions.
Comparing the three views shows whether a system lacks a capability or fails to compose capabilities it already has.
A diagnosis harness further attributes the failed episodes of three representative systems to Mind, Act, or their composition and summarizes each system in a profile card.
Our evaluation of multimodal agents , vision-language-action models (VLAs) , and world-action models (WAMs) shows that competence in a single view does not carry over to Mind2Act tasks.
Even the strongest agent succeeds in 52.7% of Mind and 39.0% of Act episodes but in only 12.0% of Mind2Act episodes.
The strongest agent retains task state but struggles with sustained contact, whereas end-to-end policies execute practiced motions but retain little task state .

items.title: Posterior Matching Distillation targets mode-covering diffusion sampling
items.summary: Posterior Matching Distillation (PMD) combines mode-covering posterior sampling with any-step generation, and its stochastic student supports any-step sampling budgets within the trained timestep grid without further training. Experiments on SDXL and FLUX.2 [klein] 4B show that PMD achieves the best FID among 4-step methods on both models while maintaining competitive or leading prompt-alignment and perceptual-quality performance.

evidence.quote: We introduce Posterior Matching Distillation (PMD) , a new member of the distribution-based distillation family that combines mode-covering posterior sampling with any-step generation .
At zero population loss , PMD recovers the teacher's full posterior of clean images at each trained noise level .
Its stochastic student supports any-step sampling budgets within the trained timestep grid without further training.
To learn these posteriors, PMD matches exponentially reweighted averages of student samples conditioned on a fixed noisy state to corresponding teacher posterior means .
We prove that, matching tilted means over an open neighborhood uniquely identifies the full posterior.
PMD thus supervises the entire conditional distribution through a family of mean constraints , without any auxiliary student-score network .

Experiments on SDXL and FLUX.2 [klein] 4B demonstrate that PMD achieves the best FID among 4-step methods on both models, while maintaining competitive or leading performance across prompt-alignment and perceptual-quality metrics .

items.title: Coda-DaVinci makes Code2Video generation task-adaptive
items.summary: Coda-DaVinci is a task-adaptive agentic framework for Code2Video generation that selects between proxy-guided and direct generation, adapts modeling granularity to each entity, and coordinates simulation with proxy-grounded prompting. Its multi-agent harness preserves scene assets and guides repairs through visual inspection and independent review, with experiments showing leading instruction following on VTR, scene consistency on R2M, and higher visual realism than the compared Code2Video baselines.

evidence.quote: Generated by deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash Code2Video uses agent-authored 3D proxies to guide video generation, enabling explicit control over structure and dynamics.
Through controlled experiments and blinded human evaluation, we study proxy granularity , physics simulation , and prompting.
The results reveal task-dependent trade-offs: coarse proxies favor natural motion, while medium-grained proxies favor consistency.
Physics simulation and proxy-aligned prompting further improve average quality.

Guided by these findings, we introduce Coda-DaVinci , a task-adaptive agentic framework for Code2Video generation that selects between proxy-guided and direct generation, adapts modeling granularity to each entity, and coordinates simulation with proxy-grounded prompting.
Its multi-agent harness preserves scene assets and guides repairs through visual inspection and independent review.

Experiments demonstrate leading instruction following on VTR and scene consistency on R2M, improved physical plausibility over direct generation, and higher visual realism than the compared Code2Video baselines.
Long-video evaluations further show gains in event structure and consistency across successive interactions, while revealing limitations in transition stability and adherence to scene settings.

items.title: Steering vectors recover most RL gains in diffusion transformers
items.summary: The authors probe RL-tuned diffusion transformers with fixed steering vectors added to the block outputs of the frozen base model, finding that on SD3.5-M these vectors hold 65x fewer parameters than the RL-tuned LoRA (0.29M against 18.8M). Identical across every prompt, token, and sampling seed, they recover 90.0-96.3% of the reward gains of six RL-tuned image models, and 89.8% and 111.9% on two RL-tuned video models, suggesting a constant shift explains most of the gain from policy-gradient RL post-training.

evidence.quote: To isolate how much of these gains an input-independent shift explains, we probe each RL-tuned model with a deliberately simple parameterization: a fixed set of steering vectors added to the block outputs of the frozen base model .
On SD3.5-M , these vectors hold 65x fewer parameters than the RL-tuned LoRA (0.29M against 18.8M).
We fit them to match the velocity predictions of public RL-tuned checkpoints , with no reward in the objective.

Although the vectors are identical for every prompt, token, and sampling seed , they recover 90.0-96.3% of the reward gains of six RL-tuned image models , and 89.8% and 111.9% on two RL-tuned video models .
Initialized at zero and trained with online RL , the vectors alone exceed the reward gains of weight-based RL on text rendering ( OCR ) and human preference ( PickScore ) on SD3.5-M .

A constant shift thus suffices for most of the gain of policy-gradient RL post-training: without new input-dependent transformations , it steers the pretrained generator toward what it can already compute.

items.title: HiUni shares one backbone for visual understanding and generation
items.summary: HiUni reuses the same language-aligned ViT and dense Transformer backbone for both visual understanding and generation, confining task-specific computation to the output side. It adds a Pixel Diffusion Head for direct pixel-space optimization and a lightweight HiGate pathway for fine-grained spatial details, achieving a similar average understanding score to the pretrained VLM with competitive image generation and editing performance.

items.title: AltRA-Test checks LLM judges without shared annotators
items.summary: AltRA-Test is a statistical test for replacing human annotators with LLM judges when items are annotated by different subsets of annotators, using a bootstrap that resamples items and substitutes one of k human annotations with an LLM annotation. Across tests of 18 LLMs and 5 prompting techniques on 20 datasets spanning text, image, audio, and video, about 100 items often suffice, and LLMs pass in about half of the real-world setups.

evidence.quote: We therefore propose the Alternative Annotator Test with Resampled Annotations (AltRA-Test) , a statistical test that does not require that all items are annotated by the same annotators.
AltRA-Test uses a bootstrap that resamples items, draws k human annotations for each item, and substitutes one of them with an LLM annotation.
This produces paired all-human and mixed human-LLM panels .

A replacement is supported when the inter-annotator agreement (IAA) of the mixed panel is statistically non-inferior to the IAA of the all-human panel, i.e., when the LLM preserves the signal that the human annotators share.
We establish that AltRA-Test is a consistent test of asymptotic level alpha .
We then evaluate it through simulations and real-world experiments in which we test 18 LLMs and 5 prompting techniques on 20 datasets across text, image, audio, and video.
Across these evaluations, about 100 items often suffice for the test.
In real-world data experiments, LLMs pass the test in about half of the setups, depending mainly on the task.
Since replacement is not always justified, we encourage researchers to test it for their task.
